preamble: Affrication of the postalveolar fricative [ʃ] to the affricate [tʃ], adding a stop closure at the same place of articulation. It is documented in Muskogean: east of the Mobile–Black Warrior line (Creek, Hitchiti-Mikasuki, Koasati and, in part, Alabama), Proto-Muskogean *š merged with *c as the affricate /tʃ/, while the Western languages Choctaw and Chickasaw keep š (Haas 1941, summarized by Hopkins).

examples.to: Creek cvse 'pumpkin', Mikasuki čoksi, Alabama and Koasati choksi
examples.note: East of the Mobile–Black Warrior line *š merged with the affricate *c (ts~ch) (Haas 1941, summarized by Hopkins); compare Choctaw shokshi, Chickasaw shokshiꞌ.

examples.to: Hitchiti čolootki, Koasati cholotka, Creek culotkv
examples.note: Compare Choctaw shʋlontʋki. Creek also has variants cvlotkv and Florida Seminole sulotkv.
Compare Choctaw shonkani. The merger has exceptions: Alabama salakla, Koasati saalakla and Creek sasakwv 'goose' (< *šalaklaka) keep s, as does Alabama sokaffi 'to peel off' (< *šokaxʷVli).
A few words keep ʃ, such as *ʃi(h) 'big' > ʃi; Copala has ʃkuu and Chicahuaxtla ʒuku.

sources: Hopkins, N. A. (2007). The Native Languages of the Southeastern United States. Foundation for the Advancement of Mesoamerican Studies. https://www.famsi.org/research/hopkins/SouthEastUSLanguages.pdf
Matsukawa, K. (2008). Reconstruction of Proto-Trique Phonemes. University of Pennsylvania Working Papers in Linguistics 14(1), 269–281. https://repository.upenn.edu/handle/20.500.14332/44671
